title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for the DeterministicFadeMem-Fusion experiment. The project is inference-only (no model training) and uses the OpenAI API (gpt-4o-mini) for answer generation and LLM-fusion baselines, plus local embedding computation. The codebase will implement a FadeMem-style memory system with swappable fusion operators (LLM-fusion, deterministic fusion, no-fusion), evaluated on the LoCoMo benchmark using the deterministic F1 protocol. Key dependencies include the OpenAI Python SDK, sentence-transformers or openai embeddings, scikit-learn for TF-IDF and cosine similarity, nltk for sentence segmentation, and the LoCoMo evaluation dataset/scripts.

steps.step1: **Base Environment Setup**: Create a local virtual environment in the working directory using Python's built-in venv module: `python -m venv .venv`. Activate with `source .venv/bin/activate`.
steps.step2: **Install Dependencies**: Install the following packages. Hardware-related: if running embeddings locally, install `torch` (check GPU model and CUDA driver version for compatible PyTorch build) and `sentence-transformers` (for local embedding fallback); otherwise, embeddings can be computed via the OpenAI API (`text-embedding-3-small`). Hardware-agnostic: `openai` (OpenAI API SDK), `scikit-learn` (TF-IDF vectorization, cosine similarity), `nltk` (sentence tokenization), `numpy`, `scipy` (bootstrap confidence intervals, paired t-tests), `pandas` (result aggregation), `matplotlib` and `seaborn` (visualization), `tqdm` (progress bars), `tiktoken` (OpenAI token counting). Install compatible versions based on the current Python environment.
steps.step3: **Clone LoCoMo Repository**: Clone the official LoCoMo benchmark repository: `git clone https://github.com/snap-research/locomo.git external/locomo`. This provides the LoCoMo dataset (`data/locomo10.json`) and reference evaluation scripts. Review the evaluation code to identify how normalized F1 partial-match is computed for the QA task (LoCoMo §4.1). Download NLTK data: `python -c "import nltk; nltk.download('punkt'); nltk.download('punkt_tab')"`.
steps.step4:
**Create Project Directory Structure**: Organize the codebase as follows:
```
dfm_fusion/
├── configs/           # YAML/JSON configuration files for each experimental condition
├── memory/            # Memory system implementation
│   ├── memory_store.py    # Core memory store (dual-layer, decay, retrieval)
│   ├── fusion_llm.py      # LLM-guided fusion operator (FadeMem-style)
│   ├── fusion_deterministic.py  # Deterministic quote-preserving fusion (ours)
│   ├── fusion_none.py     # No-fusion passthrough
│   ├── preservation.py    # Preservation checks (LLM-based and deterministic)
│   └── embeddings.py      # Embedding computation and fused-item embedding
├── data/              # Data loading and processing
│   └── locomo_loader.py   # LoCoMo dataset loader and conversation processor
├── evaluation/        # Evaluation scripts
│   ├── f1_scorer.py       # Deterministic F1 partial-match scorer (from LoCoMo §4.1)
│   └── eval_pipeline.py   # End-to-end evaluation pipeline
├── scripts/           # Shell scripts for running experiments
│   ├── setup_env.sh       # Export API keys
│   ├── run_llm_fusion.sh
│   ├── run_dfm_fusion.sh
│   └── run_no_fusion.sh
├── results/           # Raw results, logs, and analysis outputs
└── analysis/          # Analysis and visualization scripts
```
steps.step5: **Configure API Keys and Experiment Defaults**: Create `scripts/setup_env.sh` to export `OPENAI_API_KEY` (required for gpt-4o-mini answer generation and LLM-fusion calls). Create a base configuration file `configs/base_config.yaml` specifying shared settings across all conditions: embedding model (`text-embedding-3-small`), answer model (`gpt-4o-mini`, temperature=0), retrieval parameters (top-k, retrieval token budget $B_{ret}$), decay hyperparameters ($\lambda_{base}=0.1$, $\theta_{promote}=0.7$, $\theta_{demote}=0.3$, $\theta_{fusion}=0.75$, $T_{window}$), memory capacities (LML=1000, SML=500), and evaluation settings (3 runs per condition for variance estimation).

title: LLM-Fusion Baseline (FadeMem-Style) on LoCoMo
description:
Implement and evaluate the FadeMem-style LLM-guided fusion baseline in our unified evaluation harness. This baseline replicates FadeMem's core memory pipeline: dual-layer memory with decay, temporal-semantic clustering for fusion candidates, LLM-guided fusion via gpt-4o-mini, and LLM-based information preservation checking. The purpose is twofold: (1) serve as the upper-bound comparison for the proposed DeterministicFusion method, and (2) validate the harness by reproducing the directional fusion gap reported in FadeMem (LLM-Fusion >> No-Fusion). All shared components (memory store, decay, retrieval, answer generation, evaluation) are implemented here and reused by subsequent experiment items.

**Reference**: "FadeMem: Biologically-Inspired Forgetting for Efficient Agent Memory" | https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18642

steps.step1: **Data Loading and Preprocessing**: Implement `data/locomo_loader.py` to load the LoCoMo dataset from `external/locomo/data/locomo10.json`. For each of the 10 conversations: (a) parse the session structure, extracting turn-level text with speaker labels and timestamps; (b) replace image references with their BLIP captions (following LoCoMo §5 setup for text-only evaluation); (c) extract the QA pairs with their category labels (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, adversarial) and ground-truth answers; (d) extract evidence dialog IDs for retrieval recall diagnostics. Segment each conversation into chronologically ordered memory snippets (one per turn or small groups of consecutive turns from the same speaker), each annotated with a timestamp derived from the session date.
steps.step2: **Implement Core Memory Store**: Implement `memory/memory_store.py` with the FadeMem dual-layer memory architecture. Each memory item stores: content embedding $c_i$, text $s_i$, strength $v_i(t) \in [0,1]$, timestamp $\tau_i$, access frequency $f_i$, and layer assignment (LML or SML). Implement: (a) importance scoring: $I_i(t) = \alpha \cdot \text{rel}(c_i, Q_t) + \beta \cdot f_i/(1+f_i) + \gamma \cdot \exp(-\delta(t - \tau_i))$ with exponentially time-decayed access rate; (b) layer assignment with hysteresis ($\theta_{promote}=0.7$, $\theta_{demote}=0.3$); (c) decay: $v_i(t) = v_i(0) \cdot \exp(-\lambda_i \cdot (t - \tau_i)^{\beta_i})$ where $\lambda_i = \lambda_{base} \cdot \exp(-\mu \cdot I_i(t))$, $\beta_i = 0.8$ for LML, $1.2$ for SML; (d) consolidation on access: $v_i(t^+) = v_i(t) + \Delta v \cdot (1 - v_i(t)) \cdot \exp(-n_i/N)$; (e) pruning when $v_i(t) < \epsilon_{prune}$ or dormant beyond $T_{max}$ days; (f) capacities: LML=1000, SML=500. Implement retrieval: given a query, compute cosine similarity between query embedding and all active memory embeddings, return top-$k$ items.
steps.step3: **Implement Embedding Module**: Implement `memory/embeddings.py` to compute embeddings via the OpenAI API using `text-embedding-3-small`. Provide functions for: (a) embedding individual text snippets (with batching and rate-limit handling); (b) computing fused-item embeddings as the L2-normalized mean of constituent embeddings (optionally weighted by memory strength $v_i(t)$)—this is applied identically across all fusion conditions to control for retrieval confounds; (c) caching embeddings to avoid redundant API calls across runs.
steps.step4: **Implement LLM-Guided Fusion Operator**: Implement `memory/fusion_llm.py` replicating FadeMem §2.4. For each candidate memory $m_k$, form the temporal-semantic cluster: $C_k = \{m_i : \text{sim}(c_i, c_k) > \theta_{fusion} \wedge |\tau_i - \tau_k| < T_{window}\}$ where $\theta_{fusion} = 0.75$. For clusters exceeding a minimum size threshold, invoke gpt-4o-mini (temperature=0) with a prompt instructing the LLM to fuse the cluster's texts while preserving unique information, temporal progression, and causal relationships. The fused memory inherits: $v_{fused}(0) = \max_{i \in C_k} v_i(t) + \epsilon \cdot \text{var}(\{v_i\})$ (clipped to [0,1]), and reduced decay rate $\lambda_{fused} = \lambda_{base} / (1 + \log|C_k|)$. Implement the LLM-based preservation check in `memory/preservation.py`: prompt gpt-4o-mini to score information preservation between the original cluster texts and the fused text; reject fusion if preservation score < $\theta_{preserve}$. On rejection, keep the original memories unchanged.
steps.step5: **Implement Retrieval-Time Token Budget Control**: In `memory/memory_store.py`, implement the retrieval-time budget control mechanism critical for fair comparison. Define $B_{ret}$ as the total tokens appended to the answer model per query. After retrieving top-$k$ items by cosine similarity, truncate each retrieved item to $\lfloor B_{ret}/k \rfloor$ tokens (using tiktoken for token counting) before concatenation. Log the fraction of items truncated for this condition. This ensures that all conditions (LLM-Fusion, DeterministicFusion, No-Fusion) operate under the same retrieval token budget, isolating fusion quality from token-length confounds.
steps.step6: **Implement Answer Generation and Evaluation Pipeline**: Implement `evaluation/eval_pipeline.py`: for each LoCoMo QA query, (a) retrieve top-$k$ memories from the memory store under budget $B_{ret}$, (b) construct the answer prompt by appending retrieved memory texts to the query, (c) call gpt-4o-mini (temperature=0) to generate the answer, (d) log the query, retrieved memories, and generated answer. Implement `evaluation/f1_scorer.py`: compute the deterministic normalized F1 partial-match score per LoCoMo §4.1—normalize both prediction and ground truth (lowercase, remove articles/punctuation), tokenize, and compute token-level precision, recall, and F1. Report per-category F1 (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, adversarial) and overall F1. Optionally compute retrieval recall@k using evidence dialog IDs.
steps.step7: **Execute LLM-Fusion Baseline**: Run the full pipeline for the LLM-Fusion condition across all 10 LoCoMo conversations: (a) ingest conversation turns into the memory store with decay processing; (b) trigger fusion using the LLM-guided operator at appropriate intervals; (c) for each QA query, retrieve and answer under budget $B_{ret}$. Repeat for 3 runs (to capture API non-determinism variance despite temperature=0). Record: per-question multi-hop F1 scores (for paired statistical tests), overall F1, per-category F1, number of LLM fusion calls, number of accepted/rejected fusions, truncation rate of retrieved items, and total API cost/latency. Save all per-question predictions and scores to `results/llm_fusion/`.
steps.step8: **Sanity Check**: Verify that the LLM-Fusion results directionally match FadeMem's published LoCoMo multi-hop F1 of 29.43. Exact reproduction is not required (our harness may differ in minor implementation details), but the result should be in a reasonable range. If the result is drastically different (e.g., below 15 or above 45), investigate potential harness bugs before proceeding.

title: No-Fusion Ablation Baseline on LoCoMo
description:
Evaluate the No-Fusion ablation condition using the same evaluation harness. This condition keeps FadeMem's dual-layer memory with decay, conflict resolution, and retrieval entirely intact, but never triggers the fusion operator—memories are stored and retrieved individually without merging. This serves as the lower-bound comparison: FadeMem's published ablation shows that removing fusion drops multi-hop F1 from 29.43 to 13.63 (−53.7%). Reproducing this gap in our harness validates the experimental setup. The No-Fusion condition also provides the critical reference for measuring how much of the fusion gap DeterministicFusion can recover.

**Reference**: "FadeMem: Biologically-Inspired Forgetting for Efficient Agent Memory" | https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18642

steps.step1: **Implement No-Fusion Passthrough**: Implement `memory/fusion_none.py` as a trivial fusion operator that always returns the input memories unchanged (i.e., the clustering step still identifies candidates, but the fusion action is skipped). This ensures the pipeline structure is identical across conditions, differing only in the fusion operator. All other components—memory store, decay, conflict resolution, embeddings, retrieval with budget control, answer generation, and evaluation—are reused from the LLM-Fusion baseline item without modification.
steps.step2: **Execute No-Fusion Baseline**: Run the full pipeline for the No-Fusion condition across all 10 LoCoMo conversations with the same configuration as the LLM-Fusion baseline (same top-$k$, same $B_{ret}$, same answer model gpt-4o-mini at temperature=0). Repeat for 3 runs. Record: per-question multi-hop F1 scores, overall F1, per-category F1, truncation rate of retrieved items, and total API cost/latency. Note that No-Fusion uses zero additional LLM calls beyond answer generation. Save all per-question predictions and scores to `results/no_fusion/`.
steps.step3: **Validate Fusion Gap**: Compare No-Fusion results against LLM-Fusion results from the previous item. Verify that LLM-Fusion substantially outperforms No-Fusion on multi-hop F1 (directional match with FadeMem's reported gap). If the gap is negligible or reversed, the harness may have a bug (e.g., fusion not triggering correctly, or retrieval budget is too restrictive). Perform a paired t-test or paired bootstrap on per-question multi-hop F1 to confirm statistical significance of the gap.

title: DeterministicFusion (DFM-Fusion) on LoCoMo
description: Implement and evaluate the proposed DeterministicFadeMem-Fusion (DFM-Fusion) method. DFM-Fusion replaces FadeMem's LLM-guided fusion operator and LLM preservation check with a fully deterministic, quote-preserving algorithm. The fusion operator works by: (1) sentence segmentation of cluster texts using rule-based splitting, (2) near-duplicate removal via embedding similarity with threshold $\theta_{dup}$, (3) budgeted packing via deterministic MMR (maximal marginal relevance) that trades off source-strength relevance against intra-selection diversity under a per-fused-item token budget $B_{fuse}$, and (4) a deterministic preservation check based on salient-token coverage recall (numbers, capitalized entities, top-K TF-IDF tokens). All other components—memory store, dual-layer decay, conflict resolution, temporal-semantic clustering for fusion candidate identification, retrieval with budget control, embeddings, answer generation—remain identical to the LLM-Fusion baseline. The core question is whether this deterministic operator can recover most of the No-Fusion→LLM-Fusion gap on LoCoMo multi-hop F1.

steps.step1:
**Implement Deterministic Quote-Preserving Fusion Operator**: Implement `memory/fusion_deterministic.py`. The operator receives a cluster $C$ of memories (identified by the same temporal-semantic clustering as FadeMem, reused from the LLM-Fusion baseline). Processing steps:

(a) **Sentence segmentation**: Split each memory text $s_i$ in the cluster into individual sentences using NLTK's `sent_tokenize` (rule-based, no model). Each sentence retains a reference to its source memory's strength $v_i(t)$ and timestamp $\tau_i$.

(b) **Near-duplicate removal**: Compute pairwise cosine similarity between sentence embeddings (reuse cached embeddings from `memory/embeddings.py`). Greedily remove sentences whose similarity to any already-kept sentence exceeds $\theta_{dup} = 0.90$. When two sentences are near-duplicates, keep the one from the source memory with higher $v_i(t)$; break ties by preferring the more recent $\tau_i$.

(c) **Budgeted packing via deterministic MMR**: From the surviving sentences, greedily select sentences using the MMR objective: $\text{MMR}(s) = \lambda \cdot \text{strength\_score}(s) - (1 - \lambda) \cdot \max_{s' \in S_{selected}} \text{sim}(s, s')$, where $\text{strength\_score}(s) = v_i(t)$ of the sentence's source memory, and $\lambda = 0.7$ controls the relevance-diversity trade-off. Continue selecting until the cumulative token count (measured via tiktoken) reaches the per-fused-item budget $B_{fuse}$.

(d) **Emit fused text**: Concatenate selected sentences as newline-separated verbatim text, ordered by the timestamp $\tau_i$ of their source memory. Assign fused memory properties using the same formulas as FadeMem: $v_{fused}(0) = \max_{i \in C} v_i(t) + \epsilon \cdot \text{var}(\{v_i\})$ (clipped to [0,1]), $\lambda_{fused} = \lambda_{base} / (1 + \log|C|)$. Compute fused embedding as L2-normalized mean of constituent embeddings (same as LLM-Fusion condition).
steps.step2:
**Implement Deterministic Preservation Check**: Implement the deterministic coverage check in `memory/preservation.py` (extending the module from the LLM-Fusion baseline). For a candidate fused text $s_{fused}$ and its source cluster $C$:

(a) **Extract salient tokens** from the concatenation of all texts in $C$: (i) all numeric tokens (regex-matched numbers, dates, quantities), (ii) all capitalized multi-character tokens (proper nouns, named entities), (iii) top-$K$ tokens by TF-IDF score computed using scikit-learn's `TfidfVectorizer` fitted on the full conversation corpus (where $K = 20$; TF-IDF identifies rare but informative tokens in the conversation context).

(b) **Compute coverage recall**: $\text{recall} = |\text{salient\_tokens}(C) \cap \text{tokens}(s_{fused})| \;/\; |\text{salient\_tokens}(C)|$.

(c) **Accept/reject decision**: If recall $\geq \theta_{cov}$ (e.g., $\theta_{cov} = 0.85$), accept the fusion. Otherwise, reject and fall back to a safe alternative: concatenate the top-$n$ highest-strength original memories from $C$ (truncated to $B_{fuse}$ tokens total), preserving them verbatim.
steps.step3: **Create DFM-Fusion Configuration**: Create `configs/dfm_fusion_config.yaml` extending the base configuration with DFM-Fusion-specific parameters: $\theta_{dup} = 0.90$ (deduplication threshold), $\lambda_{MMR} = 0.7$ (MMR relevance-diversity trade-off), $B_{fuse}$ (per-fused-item token budget, set to match typical LLM-fusion output length observed in the LLM-Fusion baseline runs), $\theta_{cov} = 0.85$ (coverage recall threshold for preservation check), $K = 20$ (number of top TF-IDF tokens for salient token extraction). All other settings (decay, retrieval, answer model, $B_{ret}$, top-$k$) remain identical to the baseline configuration.
steps.step4: **Execute DFM-Fusion Experiment**: Run the full pipeline for the DeterministicFusion condition across all 10 LoCoMo conversations with the same setup as the baselines. The pipeline differs only in the fusion operator (deterministic instead of LLM-guided) and preservation check (coverage-based instead of LLM-based). Repeat for 3 runs (deterministic fusion itself is fully reproducible, but answer generation via gpt-4o-mini may exhibit minor API-level variance). Record: per-question multi-hop F1 scores (for paired statistical tests), overall F1, per-category F1 (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, adversarial), number of fusion events triggered, number of accepted/rejected fusions (by coverage check), truncation rate of retrieved items, and wall-clock time. DFM-Fusion should use zero additional LLM calls beyond answer generation. Save all per-question predictions and scores to `results/dfm_fusion/`.
steps.step5:
**Statistical Comparison**: Compare DFM-Fusion against both baselines using paired statistical tests on per-question multi-hop F1 scores:

(a) **DFM-Fusion vs. LLM-Fusion**: Compute paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval for the mean difference in multi-hop F1 (10,000 bootstrap resamples). Also run a paired t-test. The hypothesis is that the CI includes 0 (or the paired t-test yields $p \geq 0.05$), indicating DFM-Fusion is not statistically worse than LLM-Fusion.

(b) **DFM-Fusion vs. No-Fusion**: Compute the same paired bootstrap CI and paired t-test. The hypothesis is that DFM-Fusion is statistically significantly better than No-Fusion ($p < 0.05$).

(c) **Gap recovery metric**: Compute the fraction of the No-Fusion→LLM-Fusion gap that DFM-Fusion recovers: $\text{Gap Recovery} = (\text{F1}_{DFM} - \text{F1}_{NoFusion}) / (\text{F1}_{LLM} - \text{F1}_{NoFusion})$. Report this as a percentage.

Record all statistical test results in `results/statistical_tests.json`.

title: Success Criteria Evaluation for DFM-Fusion
description: Evaluate whether DeterministicFusion (DFM-Fusion) is effective according to the pre-specified success criteria. The core question is: can a deterministic, quote-preserving fusion operator replace FadeMem's LLM-guided fusion without statistically significant loss on LoCoMo multi-hop F1? This item collects results from all Main and Baseline Experiments, applies the three-tier decision rule (Continue/Pivot/Refute), and provides an overall effectiveness assessment. Published baseline results from FadeMem Table 3 (Fixed-16K: F1=5.17, LangChain: F1=25.75, Mem0: F1=28.37, FadeMem: F1=29.43, FadeMem w/o Fusion: F1=13.63) are also included for context.

steps.step1:
**Collect All Results**: Gather results from:
- **Main Experiment**: DFM-Fusion multi-hop F1 (mean±std over 3 runs), per-category F1, per-question scores from `results/dfm_fusion/`
- **Baseline Experiments**: LLM-Fusion multi-hop F1 (mean±std over 3 runs) from `results/llm_fusion/`, No-Fusion multi-hop F1 (mean±std over 3 runs) from `results/no_fusion/`
- **Published baselines** (cited from FadeMem Table 3, no re-run needed): Fixed-16K (F1=5.17), LangChain (F1=25.75), Mem0 (F1=28.37), FadeMem (F1=29.43), FadeMem w/o Fusion (F1=13.63)
- **Statistical tests**: Paired bootstrap CIs and paired t-test p-values from `results/statistical_tests.json`

Organize into a consolidated comparison table with columns: Method, Multi-hop F1 (mean±std), Overall F1, Source (published vs. re-run).
steps.step2:
**Apply Decision Rule**: Evaluate using the three-tier decision criteria:

(a) **Continue/Proceed**: DFM-Fusion is NOT statistically worse than LLM-Fusion (paired bootstrap 95% CI for the mean F1 difference includes 0, or paired t-test $p \geq 0.05$) AND DFM-Fusion is statistically significantly better than No-Fusion. This would confirm the hypothesis that LLM-based fusion is unnecessary for LoCoMo.

(b) **Pivot**: DFM-Fusion is statistically worse than LLM-Fusion but still significantly better than No-Fusion. This indicates that deterministic fusion captures part of the fusion benefit but not all—suggesting room for improvement (e.g., adding rule-based coreference resolution or time normalization).

(c) **Refute**: DFM-Fusion is statistically worse than LLM-Fusion AND close to or not significantly better than No-Fusion. This would imply that LLM-based rewriting/normalization is a necessary component for fusion gains on LoCoMo.

Also compute and report the gap recovery percentage: $(\text{F1}_{DFM} - \text{F1}_{NoFusion}) / (\text{F1}_{LLM} - \text{F1}_{NoFusion}) \times 100\%$.
steps.step3:
**Synthesize Effectiveness Conclusion**: Provide an overall assessment covering:
- Which decision tier (Continue/Pivot/Refute) the results fall into
- How DFM-Fusion compares against all baselines (including published ones) in absolute terms
- Per-category F1 breakdown: does DFM-Fusion match LLM-Fusion on some QA categories (e.g., single-hop, open-domain) but not others (e.g., multi-hop, temporal)? This informs which types of reasoning benefit from LLM-based fusion
- Whether the practical benefits (zero additional LLM calls, determinism, auditability) justify any small performance gap if one exists
- Overall verdict on whether the proposed idea is effective

title: Ablation Study: Coverage Check and Per-Entry Truncation
description: Ablation study to measure the contribution of two key components of DFM-Fusion: (1) the deterministic salient-token coverage check (preservation gate), and (2) the per-entry retrieval-time truncation control. Two DFM-Fusion variants are tested: one that removes the coverage check (always accepts fusions), and one that removes per-entry truncation (uses post-concatenation truncation only). Both variants are compared against the full DFM-Fusion to quantify each component's contribution to overall performance.

steps.step1:
**Define Ablation Variants**: Create two DFM-Fusion variant configurations:

(a) **DFM-Fusion w/o Coverage Check**: Modify `memory/fusion_deterministic.py` (or create a config flag) to always accept deterministic fusions regardless of the salient-token coverage recall score. All other components remain identical to full DFM-Fusion (sentence segmentation, deduplication, MMR packing, fused-item embedding).

(b) **DFM-Fusion w/o Per-Entry Truncation**: Modify the retrieval-time budget control in `memory/memory_store.py` (or create a config flag) to use post-concatenation truncation only—retrieve top-$k$ items, concatenate them in full, then truncate the concatenated text to $B_{ret}$ tokens. This removes the per-entry fairness control ($\lfloor B_{ret}/k \rfloor$ per item). All other components remain identical to full DFM-Fusion.
steps.step2: **Execute Ablation Variants**: Run each variant across all 10 LoCoMo conversations using the same configuration as the full DFM-Fusion experiment (same top-$k$, same $B_{ret}$, same answer model gpt-4o-mini at temperature=0). Run 3 runs per variant. For the w/o Coverage Check variant, additionally log: (i) the number of fusions that would have been rejected by the coverage check (i.e., fusions with coverage recall < $\theta_{cov}$), and (ii) the average coverage recall of accepted fusions. For the w/o Per-Entry Truncation variant, additionally log: (i) the fraction of queries where the first retrieved item consumes > 50% of $B_{ret}$ (indicating length dominance). Save per-question predictions and scores to `results/dfm_ablation_no_coverage/` and `results/dfm_ablation_no_truncation/`.
steps.step3:
**Compare and Analyze**: Create a comparison table:

| Variant | Multi-hop F1 (mean±std) | Δ from full DFM-Fusion |
|---------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Full DFM-Fusion | (from Main Experiment) | — |
| w/o Coverage Check | (from step 2) | ... |
| w/o Per-Entry Truncation | (from step 2) | ... |
| No-Fusion baseline | (from Baseline Experiment) | ... |

For each variant, perform a paired t-test against full DFM-Fusion on per-question multi-hop F1 to determine if the component removal causes a statistically significant drop. Analyze: (a) If w/o Coverage Check drops significantly, the coverage check prevents destructive merges where important salient information is lost. (b) If w/o Per-Entry Truncation drops significantly, the per-entry budget is important for preventing length-biased retrieval where fused items dominate the context. Save analysis to `results/ablation_analysis.json`.

title: Cost, Latency, and Fusion Statistics Analysis
description: Quantitative analysis of the practical deployment benefits of DFM-Fusion compared to LLM-Fusion. This analysis measures: (1) LLM API call reduction (number of extra LLM calls beyond answer generation), (2) wall-clock latency for the fusion stage, (3) fusion behavior statistics (cluster sizes, acceptance rates, token lengths of fused items), and (4) retrieval truncation rates across conditions. The goal is to demonstrate the cost/latency/auditability advantages of deterministic fusion even if QA performance is comparable.

steps.step1:
**Collect Operational Metrics**: From the logs of all three main conditions (LLM-Fusion, DFM-Fusion, No-Fusion), extract and tabulate:

(a) **LLM API call counts**: For each condition, count: (i) answer generation calls (should be identical: ~1,540 per run × number of runs), (ii) fusion LLM calls (LLM-Fusion only: calls for fusion generation + preservation checking), (iii) total LLM calls. Report the reduction in LLM calls for DFM-Fusion vs. LLM-Fusion as a percentage.

(b) **Wall-clock latency**: For each condition, measure total wall-clock time for: (i) the memory maintenance phase (ingestion + decay + fusion over all conversations), (ii) the QA evaluation phase (retrieval + answer generation for all questions). Report the speedup ratio for DFM-Fusion's memory maintenance vs. LLM-Fusion's.

(c) **Estimated API cost**: Using OpenAI's per-token pricing for gpt-4o-mini, estimate the total API cost for each condition (input + output tokens for all calls). Report the cost reduction for DFM-Fusion vs. LLM-Fusion.
steps.step2:
**Analyze Fusion Behavior Statistics**: Compare the fusion behavior between LLM-Fusion and DFM-Fusion:

(a) **Cluster statistics**: Distribution of cluster sizes (number of memories per fusion candidate cluster) across all conversations. Report mean, median, min, max.

(b) **Fusion acceptance rate**: For LLM-Fusion, what fraction of fusion candidates pass the LLM preservation check? For DFM-Fusion, what fraction pass the deterministic coverage check? Is one more conservative than the other?

(c) **Fused item token lengths**: Distribution of token lengths for fused items under each method. Does LLM-Fusion produce shorter/longer fused items than DFM-Fusion? How does this interact with the retrieval-time budget control?

(d) **Retrieval truncation rates**: For each condition, what fraction of retrieved items are truncated at retrieval time due to the per-entry budget $\lfloor B_{ret}/k \rfloor$? Higher truncation rates suggest the fused items are too long for the retrieval budget.
steps.step3:
**Visualize and Report**: Create the following visualizations in `analysis/`:

(a) **Bar chart**: LLM API calls by condition (stacked: answer calls + fusion calls), showing the call reduction from LLM-Fusion to DFM-Fusion.

(b) **Bar chart**: Wall-clock time comparison for memory maintenance phase across conditions.
